title: Sacagawea
summary: A Lemhi Shoshone woman captured by Hidatsa raiders as a girl, Sacagawea joined the Lewis and Clark Corps of Discovery with her husband Toussaint Charbonneau and infant son, born at Fort Mandan in February 1805. She helped the Corps find food and horses and met her Shoshone brother in summer 1805. She and her family left the expedition at the Hidatsa-Mandan villages in August 1806.

uncertainty.note: Both dates are circa. The NPS gives c. 1788 for birth; death c. 1812 at Fort Manuel Lisa is described as generally thought.

where.modern_name: Knife River Indian Villages National Historic Site, Stanton, Mercer County, North Dakota (pinned to the Mandan and Hidatsa villages where she lived and joined the Corps; born in Lemhi County, Idaho)
where.historical_name: Mandan and Hidatsa villages, North Dakota (the NPS page names the Awatixa (Sakakawea) Village)

importance.justification: The only woman in the Corps of Discovery, valued for her knowledge of tribes and terrain and her Shoshone connections.

sources.title: OpenStreetMap Nominatim result for Knife River Indian Villages NHS

reviewer_note: Pin is the village area, not the exact site of Fort Mandan, which neither opened page locates. Her later life and death are poorly documented; the NPS page says little is known. No path animation: waypoint coordinates were not sourced.
